entities.name: Stabat Mater
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: Stabat Mater is a seminal literary work created by Jacopone da Todi in the 13th century, specifically between 1264 and 1275, in what is now Umbria, Italy. This iconic text, which translates to 'The Stabbing of the Virgin', has had a profound impact on Christian devotion and spirituality, with its vivid depiction of Mary's suffering and death influencing artistic and liturgical expression for centuries to come. The work's significance extends beyond its literary merit, as it reflects the cultural and theological currents of the late Middle Ages, including the rise of Franciscan spirituality and the influence of the Catholic Church. Stabat Mater has also been a source of inspiration for countless musicians, artists, and writers, cementing its place in the cultural heritage of Western civilization.
